message.content:
I need to find where memo metadata is computed/derived from memo content in this repository. This is metadata used for lists/previews that is extracted from the memo's content rather than set by the user. Search very thoroughly for:

1. Any code that computes or extracts metadata from memo content (e.g., snippets, titles, excerpts, word counts, etc.)
2. Look for functions or methods that parse memo content to derive properties
3. Search for terms like "snippet", "excerpt", "preview", "metadata", "extract", "derive", "compute" in relation to memos
4. Check for any memo model/store that has computed or derived fields

Search breadth: very thorough. Report exact file paths and line numbers.

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

---

## Memo Metadata Derived from Content -- Complete Findings

There are two distinct systems that compute/derive metadata from memo content in this repository:

---

### 1. Payload Properties (tags, structural booleans, title) -- persisted to the database

**Proto definition of the derived payload:**

- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/memo.proto` (lines 7-22) -- Defines `MemoPayload.Property` with fields: `has_link`, `has_task_list`, `has_code`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, `title`. Also stores extracted `tags` (line 13).

**Core extraction logic (single-pass AST walk):**

- `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`
  - Lines 20-25: `ExtractedData` struct -- holds `Tags []string`, `Mentions []string`, `Property *storepb.MemoPayload_Property`.
  - Lines 356-422: `ExtractAll()` -- The primary single-pass extraction function. Walks the goldmark AST once and collects:
    - **Tags** (line 377): `#tag` nodes, deduplicated (line 418).
    - **Mentions** (line 380): `@mention` nodes, lowercased.
    - **Title** (lines 384-388): Extracted from the first block-level child of the document if it is an H1 heading.
    - **HasLink** (line 394): True when any `KindLink` node is found.
    - **HasCode** (lines 396): True when any `KindCodeBlock`, `KindFencedCodeBlock`, or `KindCodeSpan` is found.
    - **HasTaskList** (line 399): True when any `KindTaskCheckBox` is found.
    - **HasIncompleteTasks** (lines 401-403): True when an unchecked task checkbox is found.
  - Lines 193-241: `ExtractProperties()` -- Standalone version that extracts only the boolean properties and title (same logic as `ExtractAll` but without tags/mentions).
  - Lines 142-170: `ExtractTags()` -- Standalone tag extraction.

**Where extraction is triggered (payload rebuild):**

- `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`
  - Lines 74-87: `RebuildMemoPayload()` -- Calls `markdownService.ExtractAll(memo.Content)` and sets `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property` from the extracted data.
  - Lines 27-65: `Runner.RunOnce()` -- Batch rebuilds payload for all memos in the database (migration/repair tool).

- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`
  - Line 108: Called during `CreateMemo` -- `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService)`.
  - Line 447: Called during `UpdateMemo` when content changes -- `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService)`.

**Conversion to API response:**

- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`
  - Lines 48-49: Maps stored `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property` into the API response.
  - Lines 315-326: `convertMemoPropertyFromStore()` -- Converts `storepb.MemoPayload_Property` to `v1pb.Memo_Property`.

---

### 2. Snippet (plain-text preview) -- computed on the fly, not persisted

**Proto definition:**

- `/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`
  - Lines 265-266: `string snippet = 17` marked `OUTPUT_ONLY` on the `Memo` message.
  - Lines 443-444: `string snippet = 2` marked `OUTPUT_ONLY` on `MemoRelation.Memo`.

**Core snippet generation:**

- `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`
  - Lines 263-346: `GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int)` -- Walks the AST to produce a plain-text summary:
    - Skips code blocks (lines 276-278).
    - Adds space between block elements (lines 284-301).
    - Extracts text from `Text`, `AutoLink`, and `TagNode` nodes (lines 308-324).
    - Stops early if buffer exceeds 2x maxLength (lines 326-328).
    - Truncates at word boundary via `truncateAtWord()` (lines 341-342, 472-488).

**Where snippet generation is called:**

- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`
  - Lines 83-90: `getMemoContentSnippet()` -- Thin wrapper that calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(content, 64)` with a max length of 64 characters.

- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`
  - Lines 76-80: Called in `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators()` to set `memoMessage.Snippet` on every memo API response.
  - Lines 221-254: Called in `batchConvertMemoRelations()` to set `Snippet` on related memo references.

- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`
  - Lines 149-176: `convertMemoRelationFromStore()` -- Generates snippets for both sides of a memo relation.

- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go`
  - Lines 318-328: `memoNotificationSnippet()` -- Generates snippets for notification payloads.
  - Lines 346-359: Snippets for comment notifications (`MemoCommentPayload.MemoSnippet`, `RelatedMemoSnippet`).
  - Lines 374-391: Snippets for mention notifications (`MemoMentionPayload.MemoSnippet`, `RelatedMemoSnippet`).

---

### 3. RSS title extraction -- computed on the fly

- `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go`
  - Lines 302-336: `generateItemTitle()` -- Extracts the first line of memo content, strips markdown heading syntax via regex (`markdownHeadingRegex`, line 31), truncates to 100 chars at word boundary, defaults to "Memo" if empty.
  - Lines 338-344: `getRSSItemDescription()` -- Renders full memo content to HTML via `s.MarkdownService.RenderHTML()`.
  - Lines 243-248: Both are used in `generateRSSFromMemoList()` to populate RSS feed items.

---

### 4. Mention extraction -- computed on memo create/update

- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`
  - Lines 26-38: `resolveMentionTargets()` -- Calls `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll()` to get `data.Mentions` from content, then resolves usernames to users.
  - Lines 91-146: `dispatchMemoMentionNotifications()` -- Uses the above to diff current vs. previous mentions and send inbox notifications.

---

### 5. Frontend consumption of derived metadata

The frontend does not itself compute metadata from content; it consumes the server-derived fields:

- `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoView/components/MemoSnippetLink.tsx` (lines 13-34): Renders the `snippet` field as a truncated link label.
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoMetadata/Relation/RelationCard.tsx` (line 12): Passes `memo.snippet` to `MemoSnippetLink`.
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/UserMemoMap/UserMemoMap.tsx` (line 154): Displays `memo.snippet` on the map view.
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/Inbox/MemoCommentMessage.tsx` (lines 132, 147): Displays `memoSnippet`/`relatedMemoSnippet`.
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/Inbox/MemoMentionMessage.tsx` (lines 135, 153): Displays mention notification snippets.
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/contexts/MemoFilterContext.tsx` (lines 11-13): Filter factors `property.hasLink`, `property.hasTaskList`, `property.hasCode`.
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/hooks/useMemoFilters.ts` (lines 73-78): Translates property filter factors into server filter conditions.

---

### Summary of all derived metadata fields

| Derived Field | Source | Persisted? | Where Computed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tags` | `#tag` nodes in markdown | Yes (in `MemoPayload`) | `ExtractAll()` via `RebuildMemoPayload()` |
| `property.has_link` | Presence of link nodes | Yes (in `MemoPayload.Property`) | `ExtractAll()` via `RebuildMemoPayload()` |
| `property.has_task_list` | Presence of task checkboxes | Yes | Same |
| `property.has_code` | Presence of code blocks/spans | Yes | Same |
| `property.has_incomplete_tasks` | Presence of unchecked checkboxes | Yes | Same |
| `property.title` | First H1 heading text | Yes | Same |
| `mentions` | `@user` nodes in markdown | Not persisted (used to dispatch notifications) | `ExtractAll()` in `resolveMentionTargets()` |
| `snippet` | Plain-text truncation of content (64 chars) | No (computed on every API response) | `GenerateSnippet()` via `getMemoContentSnippet()` |
| RSS `title` | First line of content, heading syntax stripped | No (computed per RSS request) | `generateItemTitle()` |
| RSS `description` | Full HTML rendering | No | `getRSSItemDescription()` via `RenderHTML()` |
